title: Add the requirements
body: T21 from Factory v0: docs/requirements.md, generated from docs/product-brief.md. Numbered functional and non-functional requirements that later planning steps cite by ID, a traceability table from the brief's success criteria, and open questions for Human Gate #1. No code.

change.prompt:
Write the requirements for this app from docs/product-brief.md. Create only docs/requirements.md. Do not change any other file, including the brief, and do not write code.

The requirements feed the next planning steps: architecture, data model, API and security decisions, acceptance tests, and a task graph of independent build tasks. Then comes Human Gate #1, where the operator answers the open questions. Acceptance tests and build tasks will cite requirements by ID, so each requirement says what the app must do in a way an automated test could observe, not how it is built.

Rules:
- The source is docs/product-brief.md only. Do not widen its Scope. Do not read or cite the vendored skills in .agents/ or .claude/.
- Where the brief conflicts with itself, follow its Assumptions. Its Target users mentions a small team, but its Assumptions make each project belong to one user, with one kind of account. Write the requirements for single-owner projects.
- The brief's Scope lets a user create, list, and open projects. Renaming and deleting projects are not v1 requirements. List them under Out of scope, and note that the brief's assumption (deleting a project deletes its tasks) applies if deletion is added later.
- Turn the brief's Assumptions into requirements where they apply. Priorities are Low, Medium, and High, and new tasks default to Medium. New tasks start as Todo. A task belongs to one project. The dashboard counts tasks across all of the user's projects.
- Where a requirement needs a detail the brief leaves open, choose the simplest reasonable option, write it into the requirement, and list it under Assumptions. Examples are name and title length limits, the order of lists, and what an empty list shows.
- Do not decide persistence, the database, the sign-in method or provider, hosting, or cloud architecture. Do not name any database, ORM, auth library or protocol, sign-in method (such as passwords, passkeys, magic links, SSO, or MFA), hosting platform, or cloud service, not even to rule one out. Say what the product needs, for example that a user must be signed in to see any project or task, and leave the method to Open questions.
- Plain English and short sentences, 800 to 2400 words. No marketing language, no placeholders (TBD, TODO, FIXME, lorem), and no emoji.

Use exactly these headings in this order, with no other level-1 or level-2 headings, and put a blank line after every heading:

# Requirements: Agent Factory Benchmark
## Overview: two or three sentences. Say that the source is docs/product-brief.md and that later planning documents cite requirements by ID.
## Functional requirements: grouped under these level-3 headings, in this order: Access, Projects, Tasks, Status and priority, Filtering, Dashboard.
## Non-functional requirements: 4 to 10, covering at least access control (enforced on every read and change, not only hidden in the interface), input validation, accessibility, error and empty states, and testability.
## Traceability
## Out of scope: point to the brief's Non-goals rather than repeating them all, and add what this document leaves out, such as renaming and deleting projects.
## Assumptions: a bulleted list of only the new assumptions this document makes, at least 2.
## Open questions: a bulleted list of 3 to 8 questions for the operator at Human Gate #1.

The heading lines themselves are only the text before the colon, for example "## Overview".

Requirements:
- One bullet per requirement, on one line, in the form: - **FR-01** A signed-in user must be able to create a project by giving it a name.
- Number functional requirements FR-01, FR-02, and so on, and non-functional ones NFR-01, NFR-02, and so on, in order with no gaps and always two digits. Write 12 to 30 functional requirements.
- Each requirement is one behaviour an automated test could check, and uses the word must.
- Every bullet in the two requirement sections is a requirement. Put any explanation in a plain sentence, not a bullet.
- Only cite requirement IDs that exist.

Traceability: one Markdown table with the columns ID, Brief success criterion, and Requirements. Add one row per bullet in the brief's Success criteria, in the same order. The ID is SC-1, SC-2, and so on. Paraphrase the criterion briefly, and list the IDs of the requirements that together satisfy it, for example | SC-1 | Create a project and see it listed | FR-04, FR-05 |.

Open questions: carry over the brief's open questions that are still open, and merge the ones that ask the same thing (the brief's first and fifth questions both ask about sharing). Add questions the requirements raise, such as how users sign in (without naming a method) and whether a user can delete their account and data. Each bullet is one line. It starts with the IDs of the requirements its answer would change, in parentheses, and ends with a question mark, for example: - (FR-04, NFR-01) Should projects ever be shared between accounts?

When you finish, run every verify command listed below yourself, and fix whatever fails.

verify:
python3 -c 'import re; t = open("docs/requirements.md", encoding="utf-8").read(); L = t.splitlines(); sec = {}; cur = None
for l in L:
    if l.startswith("## "): cur = l[3:]; sec[cur] = []
    elif cur: sec[cur].append(l)
body = lambda s: "\n".join(sec[s])
bullets = lambda s: [l for l in sec[s] if re.match(r"([-*]|\d+\.) ", l)]
want = ["# Requirements: Agent Factory Benchmark", "## Overview", "## Functional requirements", "## Non-functional requirements", "## Traceability", "## Out of scope", "## Assumptions", "## Open questions"]
assert L[0] == want[0], "title"
heads = [l for l in L if re.match(r"#{1,2} ", l)]; assert heads == want, heads
bad = [l for i, l in enumerate(L) if l.startswith("#") and (i + 1 >= len(L) or L[i + 1] != "")]; assert not bad, ("no blank line after", bad)
n = len(t.split()); assert 800 <= n <= 2400, f"{n} words"
assert not re.search(r"\b(TBD|TODO|FIXME)\b", t) and "lorem" not in t.lower(), "placeholder"
assert not re.search("[\U0001F300-\U0001FAFF\u2600-\u27BF]", t), "emoji"
'

python3 -c 'import re; t = open("docs/requirements.md", encoding="utf-8").read(); L = t.splitlines(); sec = {}; cur = None
for l in L:
    if l.startswith("## "): cur = l[3:]; sec[cur] = []
    elif cur: sec[cur].append(l)
body = lambda s: "\n".join(sec[s])
bullets = lambda s: [l for l in sec[s] if re.match(r"([-*]|\d+\.) ", l)]
fb = bullets("Functional requirements"); nb = bullets("Non-functional requirements")
assert all(re.match(r"- \*\*FR-\d{2}\*\* \S", l) for l in fb), [l for l in fb if not re.match(r"- \*\*FR-\d{2}\*\* \S", l)]
assert all(re.match(r"- \*\*NFR-\d{2}\*\* \S", l) for l in nb), [l for l in nb if not re.match(r"- \*\*NFR-\d{2}\*\* \S", l)]
f = [l[4:9] for l in fb]; nf = [l[4:10] for l in nb]
assert 12 <= len(f) <= 30 and f == [f"FR-{i:02d}" for i in range(1, len(f) + 1)], f
assert 4 <= len(nf) <= 10 and nf == [f"NFR-{i:02d}" for i in range(1, len(nf) + 1)], nf
assert all(re.search(r"\bmust\b", l) for l in fb + nb), [l for l in fb + nb if not re.search(r"\bmust\b", l)]
used = set(re.findall(r"\bN?FR-\d+\b", t)); assert used <= set(f + nf), ("unknown IDs", used - set(f + nf))
'

python3 -c 'import re; t = open("docs/requirements.md", encoding="utf-8").read(); L = t.splitlines(); sec = {}; cur = None
for l in L:
    if l.startswith("## "): cur = l[3:]; sec[cur] = []
    elif cur: sec[cur].append(l)
body = lambda s: "\n".join(sec[s])
bullets = lambda s: [l for l in sec[s] if re.match(r"([-*]|\d+\.) ", l)]
b = open("docs/product-brief.md", encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n## ")
sc = [x for x in b if x.startswith("Success criteria\n")][0]; nsc = len([l for l in sc.splitlines() if re.match(r"[-*] ", l)]); assert nsc >= 5, nsc
rows = [[c.strip() for c in l.strip().strip("|").split("|")] for l in sec["Traceability"] if l.startswith("| SC-")]
assert [r[0] for r in rows] == [f"SC-{i}" for i in range(1, nsc + 1)], ("one row per brief success criterion", [r[0] for r in rows])
assert all(len(r) == 3 and re.search(r"\bN?FR-\d{2}\b", r[2]) for r in rows), "each row names a requirement"
fr = body("Functional requirements")
for w in ["Todo", "In Progress", "Done", "Low", "Medium", "High"]: assert re.search(r"\b" + w + r"\b", fr), w
assert re.search(r"sign(ed)?[ -]?in", fr, re.I), "sign-in"
m = sorted({x.group(0) for x in re.finditer(r"assignee|due date|attachment|notification|\bcomments?\b|sub-?tasks?\b|\blabels?\b|\btags?\b", fr, re.I)}); assert not m, ("non-goals", m)
assert len(bullets("Assumptions")) >= 2, "assumptions"
q = bullets("Open questions"); assert 3 <= len(q) <= 8 and all(l.rstrip().endswith("?") and re.search(r"\bN?FR-\d{2}\b", l) for l in q), q
'

python3 -c 'import re; t = open("docs/requirements.md", encoding="utf-8").read(); L = t.splitlines(); sec = {}; cur = None
for l in L:
    if l.startswith("## "): cur = l[3:]; sec[cur] = []
    elif cur: sec[cur].append(l)
body = lambda s: "\n".join(sec[s])
bullets = lambda s: [l for l in sec[s] if re.match(r"([-*]|\d+\.) ", l)]
bad = r"\b(postgres(ql)?|mysql|mariadb|sqlite|dynamo(db)?|mongo(db)?|prisma|drizzle|supabase|firebase|redis|cognito|auth0|clerk|next-?auth|auth\.js|lucia|oauth|oidc|saml|jwt|lambda|fargate|ecs|eks|ec2|amplify|s3|rds|aurora|aws|azure|gcp|vercel|netlify|heroku|docker|kubernetes|graphql|trpc|passwords?|passkeys?|magic[ -]links?|sso|single sign-on|mfa|2fa|two-factor)\b"

'
